argument:
Alphabet's 30% operating-income growth, 34.03% operating margin and 82% Cloud revenue growth establish an operating thesis independent of the $97.983bn other-income windfall. TTM FCF of $53.273bn and $242.474bn cash/securities provide funding capacity despite heavy investment. Continued Cloud and broader operating growth could support attractive ownership at the estimated 23.07x forward multiple.

Quarterly FCF was negative $5.855bn, H1 FCF only $4.261bn, and the $49.6bn equity raise dilutes per-share participation. Liquid assets exceed disclosed long-term debt, but that is not an all-in net-debt calculation. The 17.38x trailing multiple is distorted by unrealised gains and cannot carry the argument. Positive TTM cash and recurring operating progress make the risks manageable conditionally, provided AI investment earns returns. Weak-volume recovery does not establish a tactical breakout.
key_points: Operating growth survives removal of investment-gain headline earnings.
Positive TTM FCF and liquidity offer investment capacity.
Negative quarterly cash and dilution require per-share return discipline.
